title: Explain Any Codebase
tagline: From inherited repo to readable wiki
outro: Docs that keep up with the code.
script: You've inherited a codebase. Two hundred thousand lines, three READMEs, all stale. IronClaw's move: point the agent at the repo. It maps the code into a knowledge graph — files, symbols, and the connections between them — then reads its way through with file tools and writes what it finds: architecture overviews, setup guides, how the pieces actually fit. Not autogenerated API dumps — narrative docs, exported as plain Markdown you can commit next to the code. And this isn't hypothetical: IronClaw's own repo keeps a wiki exactly like this — regenerated every week in CI, opened as a pull request, and reviewed by humans before merge. Point. Index. Explain. Docs that keep up with the code.
